nodes.name: Dynamic H2 Bubble Template Deposition of NiW
nodes.procedure: Using a dynamic H2 bubble template (DHBT) method, NiW bimetallic alloys were uniformly deposited on a NM substrate. During this process, Ni2+ and WO4 2- ions are co-reduced onto the NM substrate, resulting in a porous NiW bimetallic alloy architecture.

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: DHBT utilizes a high cathodic current density that simultaneously accelerates metal ion reduction and induces vigorous H2 evolution on the conductive NM substrate.

nodes.source_text: Using a dynamic H2 bubble template (DHBT) method, NiW bimetallic alloys were uniformly deposited on a NM substrate... resulting in a porous NiW bimetallic alloy architecture.

nodes.name: DHBT Synthesis of Monometallic PN
nodes.procedure: The monometallic PN electrocatalyst was synthesized following the same DHBT method as the NiW alloy but in the absence of WO4 2- ions.

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The absence of WO42- ions led to the formation of aggregated Ni particles for the monometallic PN electrocatalyst.

nodes.source_text: The absence of WO42- ions led to the formation of aggregated Ni particles with larger sizes for the monometallic PN electrocatalyst

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD confirms the fcc Ni structure for NiW and PN, and bcc W for WM, with no Ni- or W-based oxide phases detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns ... correspond to the (111), (200), and (220) crystal planes of face centered cubic (fcc) Ni ... absence of characteristic diffraction peaks corresponding to Ni- and W-based oxides in the magnified XRD patterns (Figure S6, Supporting Information) provides additional evidence for the successful formation of the NiW bimetallic alloy.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS identifies metallic Ni0 and W0 as dominant surface states, with binding energy shifts suggesting electron transfer from Ni to W.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS survey spectra confirm the presence of Ni and W ... Ni 2p XPS spectrum of the porous NiW bimetallic alloy exhibits a positive binding energy shift relative to the monometallic PN, whereas the W 4f XPS spectrum shows a negative shift compared to the monometallic WM. These shifts in binding energy suggests that electrons are transferred from the less electronegative Ni to the more electronegative W ...

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni K-edge XANES spectra show the Ni valence state in NiW is nearly metallic Ni0.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ni K-edge XANES spectra reveal that the valence state of Ni in the porous NiW bimetallic alloy closely resembles that of metallic Ni0 in Ni foil, indicating minimal oxidation (Figure 2c).

properties.description: XANES spectrum showing the Ni K-edge for various samples and reference materials.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT and WT EXAFS profiles confirm Ni-Ni/W coordination and the absence of Ni-O bonding in the NiW alloy.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fourier transform (FT) and wavelet transform (WT) profiles of the Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra (Figure 2d-f ... display prominent Ni-Ni/W coordination features while lacking signals attributable to Ni-O-Ni or Ni-O bonds ...

nodes.characterization_summary: Nyquist and Bode plots show the NiW catalyst has the lowest interfacial resistance and smallest phase angles, indicating superior electron and mass transport.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Nyquist plots, the porous NiW bimetallic alloy electrocatalyst exhibits a smaller semicircle diameter than monometallic PN, monometallic WM, and RN electrocatalysts ... the porous NiW alloy electrocatalyst shows the smallest phase angle at each overpotential, reflecting its strong mass transfer capability ...

nodes.characterization_summary: The ECSA of the NiW alloy was measured to be 97.6 cm2, significantly higher than its monometallic counterparts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The porous NiW bimetallic alloy electrocatalyst exhibits the largest ECSA of 97.6 cm2 (Figure S16, Supporting Information), significantly surpassing that of the monometallic PN (0.9 cm2) ...

nodes.characterization_summary: Water contact angle measurements show the NiW alloy is highly hydrophilic (28.5°), aiding electrolyte permeation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: porous NiW bimetallic alloy electrocatalyst exhibits the smallest water contact angle of 28.5°, compared to monometallic PN (30.1°), monometallic WM (95.7°), RN (85.7°), and NM (101.7°) electrocatalysts, indicating superior hydrophilicity.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ ATR-SEIRAS shows red shifts in H2O-related bands, indicating weakened O-H bonds and facilitated water dissociation on the NiW surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with monometallic Ni and W, the delta (H - OH) band of the porous NiW bimetallic alloy exhibits a noticeable red shift, indicative of O-H bond elongation and weakened bond strength. This implies that H2O molecule dissociates more readily on the NiW bimetallic alloy surface ...

nodes.characterization_summary: DFT calculations reveal that alloying Ni with W shifts the d-band center of the W 5d orbital downward, promoting OH intermediate desorption.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Theoretical studies reveal that alloying Ni with W shifts the d-band center (epsilon_d) of the W 5d orbital downward, which enhances *OH intermediate desorption and promotes H2O adsorption and dissociation at the W site ...

nodes.evidence_snippet: the porous NiW bimetallic alloy electrocatalyst demonstrates a small Tafel slope of 117 mV dec-1 lower than that of monometallic PN (130 mV dec-1), monometallic WM (135 mV dec-1), RN (130 mV dec-1), NM (183 mV dec-1) ... indicating enhanced reaction kinetics (Figure 3d).
